subject: BrightWave: RTBF & backup purge playbook — follow-up and ask
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@brightwave.health>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@brightwave.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: BrightWave: RTBF & backup purge playbook — follow-up and ask

Hi Sophie / Tom —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the immediate asks we agreed on: 

- Scope: customer-facing PII from user prompts + metadata (timestamps, user IDs). No PHI ingestion is planned today; you confirmed filters will be applied before ingestion.
- Retention: BrightWave needs the ability to flag and delete user accounts on request (RTBF) with a target purge window of 30 days for active storage and 90 days for snapshot/backups.
- Logging: You require detailed audit logs for deletions (requestor, timestamp, objects removed) retained for 1 year.
- Residency: Production workloads live in us-east-1; backups currently cross-region to us-west-2 — you want options to keep backups in-region only.

Next steps I promised:
1) Send a light RTBF playbook that maps Redwood deletion steps to your requirements (what we can automate vs. manual steps for backups).
2) Share our logging schema for audit trails and an example retention configuration.
3) Provide an initial qualification checklist we can use to confirm whether any BrightWave data falls under special retention/archival rules.

Attaching: BrightWave_DLP_Qs.xlsx (your DLP export) and a first-draft Redwood_RTBF_Playbook_v1.pdf.

Can you confirm whether the 30/90-day windows are firm targets or negotiable margins? Also flag any legal/regulatory constraints I should know about (state-level requirements or contract clauses).

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marissa for pricing/SLAs once we agree on scope.

—Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0122

From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@brightwave.health>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@brightwave.health>, BrightWave Security <security@brightwave.health>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 16:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: BrightWave: RTBF & backup purge playbook — follow-up and ask

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- 30/90 are internal targets — legal prefers 45/120 if engineering can't guarantee no snapshot traces earlier. We need a clear description of where "purge" stops (logical delete vs. crypto-erase).
- Backups: we cannot cross-region backups for certain datasets containing state-level regulated lab results; those need in-region-only.
- Audit logs: 1 year is fine, but we also need atomic deletion events for any RTBF operation (request id, user id, model version, affected blob ids).

Tom (security) is looping in our compliance counsel; they'll send any contract language they want included.

Can you also confirm whether Redwood can expose a deletion webhook/callback so we can update our CRM flags? That would be very helpful.

—Sophie
Director, Platform Engineering | BrightWave Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 03:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightWave: RTBF & backup purge playbook — follow-up and ask

Alex / Marissa —

Summary of technical constraints and suggested language we can share with BrightWave: 

1) Live deletion: Redwood can perform a full logical purge of active object stores and KV caches within a rolling 30–45 day window depending on the workflows they prefer. We will preserve an audit record (immutable event entry) and can push deletion events to a customer webhook endpoint with a guaranteed delivery-at-least-once semantics. Example webhook schema attached.

2) Snapshots/backups: For backups, we do not have an automatic crypto-erase across vendor-managed backup systems today; operationally we can: 
   - Provide a documented manual purge playbook for snapshots with a 90–120 day target, or
   - Offer a Dedicated/Private deployment option where backups can be constrained to a single region and encrypted with a customer-managed KMS that supports key destruction for stronger guarantees.

3) Logging: Attached 'rtbf_deletion_log_schema.json' (sample) — it contains request_id, actor, timestamp, data_objects_affected[], model_version, retention_policy_applied. We can commit to 1 year retention for audit logs under our standard SLA; longer retention is an add-on.

Attachments in my reply: example_webhook_payload.json (sample), rtbf_deletion_log_schema.json (sample).

If BrightWave needs crypto-erase guarantees for backups as part of a regulated workflow, we should push Private deployment/KMS as the path forward and mark it as a procurement trigger.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Sophie / Tom —

Thanks for the quick reply and context. Putting Karthik's notes into plain next steps so we can lock scope: 

- Production deletion window: we can commit to "logical purge" of active storage within 45 days. If you need the 30-day target we should add a performance SLA and a cost uplift.
- Backups/snapshots: for the regulated datasets that must remain in-region, we recommend Private or Dedicated with regional-only replication + customer KMS; otherwise, we provide a manual snapshot purge playbook targeting 120 days.
- Audit logs & webhook: we will provide the deletion event webhook (at-least-once). Karthik attached sample payload and the RTBF log schema. We can retain audit logs 1 year by default.

Attached is a short playbook PDF that maps the steps and responsibilities (Redwood vs BrightWave) and an initial pricing note we'll formalize once you confirm the retention windows.

Requested from you: confirm whether BrightWave will accept the 45/120 windows as an initial contract baseline, and share any export guidance your compliance counsel provides. Also, please confirm the webhook endpoint we should use (format: https://hooks.brightwave.health/redwood/rtbf).

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute follow-up with Marissa and Karthik next week to walk through the playbook and cost options.

Best —
Alex Martinez
